 Karla Demery is a travel journalist who specializes in investigative reporting. Her passion for uncovering how culture, history, and travel intersect began while living in South Korea and traveling throughout Asia for four years. Since then, she has returned to the United States and now reports on how current events shape the travel experience around the country. In addition to reporting the news, Karla loves to tell stories about America’s most fascinating places.
Prior to contributing to TheTravel, Karla wrote travel and lifestyle pieces for Trip101 and College Fashionista. When she is not writing, she can often be found trying new cuisines or planning her next trip.

 Flying straight to Tulum from the United States was supposed to make reaching Mexico’s Riviera Maya easier for American vacationers. Instead of landing in Cancún and continuing south by car, travelers could arrive at an airport built to serve the destination. But less than three years after opening, two major U.S. airlines, United and Delta, are canceling flights to Tulum's Felipe Carrillo Puerto International Airport (TQO).

 The route cuts follow earlier withdrawals by other carriers. However, passengers with Tulum vacations booked still have ways to reach their hotels, even if their original flights disappear.

 Delta Air Lines Will Suspend Its Tulum Route In May 2027
 Tulum International Airport, Tulum, Quintana Roo, Mexico Credit: George Wirt / Shutterstock.com 
 Delta’s Atlanta–Tulum route will stop operating beginning May 3, 2027 , according to an airline statement reported by Riviera Maya News . With its Detroit and Minneapolis-St. Paul routes to Tulum already dropped, the latest suspension will leave Delta without any flights to Tulum at all.
 The decision is a big shift from Delta’s original plans for daily, year-round Atlanta–Tulum service , which launched on March 28, 2024. At the time, the airline promoted the route as a way for travelers to reach Tulum without the drive from Cancún.
 For now, passengers can still fly the Atlanta route through the winter and into spring, although service will run less frequently during part of that period.
 "Daily scheduled flights between Atlanta and Tulum will operate from November 22, 2026, to May 2, 2027, with the exception of the period from January 12 to March 3, during which there will be no flights on Tuesdays or Wednesdays," the airline stated.
 Delta has also canceled the Saturday-only flights it previously planned for the May–July 2027 period. Instead, travelers will have to wait until later in the year for the airline’s expected return.
 "Delta flights to TQO (Tulum) from ATL (Atlanta) are scheduled to resume in November 2027. The service to Tulum will then operate on a seasonal basis," the airline continued.
 An exact restart date has not been announced. United Airlines, meanwhile, previously confirmed it will end its remaining Tulum flights months earlier than Delta, in January 2027.
 United Airlines Is Leaving Tulum As Other Airlines Cut Back
 United Airlines aircraft at Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR), New Jersey, USA Credit: George Wirt / Shutterstock.com 
 United’s last Newark–Tulum flight is scheduled for January 2, 2027 , followed by its final Houston–Tulum flight on January 4 . The airline confirmed those dates to The Points Guy , which also reported that United had already decided to end its Chicago and Los Angeles routes .
 United said it adjusts its schedule based on seasonality, demand, and other market factors. The departure comes as the airline adds 10 international destinations for 2027 in its largest overseas expansion .

 Tulum’s airport opened on December 1, 2023 , initially handling only domestic flights until international arrivals began on March 28, 2024 . However, the airport has struggled to retain the network it had when it opened. JetBlue has also pulled out, while other airlines have reduced or suspended service.
 Aeroméxico operated its last Tulum flights on September 30, 2026, describing the suspension as temporary and citing market conditions. Volaris plans to suspend operations beginning January 7, 2027, after reviewing the profitability of routes with lower passenger loads, according to TravelPulse .
 While it's not confirmed exactly what these flight reductions mean for the airport, it does mean that travelers who had existing reservations will need to make other arrangements.
 Options For Passengers With Affected Tulum Bookings
 Parking area at Cancun International Airport, Mexico Credit: Fotos593 / Shutterstock.com 
 United is offering affected passengers the option to change their reservations to nearby airports, including Cancún International Airport (CUN), or request a refund. So, those booked from Newark or Houston should contact the carrier to review replacement itineraries before purchasing another ticket themselves.
 "Customers will have the option to change their reservation to flights to nearby airports, such as Cancun (CUN), which is between 1.5 and 2 hours away by car and serves many of the same tourist areas as TQO; alternatively, they can request a refund," the carrier told El Financiero .
 Additionally, Delta’s schedule-change policy says it will attempt to rebook passengers automatically where possible. Those unhappy with the replacement can review other flights through My Trips or the Fly Delta app, contact the airline for assistance, or cancel for a refund of their unused transportation. Passengers hoping to keep their Tulum vacation can also ask about switching to Atlanta–Cancún, which appears in Delta Vacations’ flight schedule .
 Reaching Tulum after landing in Cancún is still possible, but travelers will need to plan for about two hours on the road, depending on traffic and their hotel’s location.
 A private or hotel-arranged transfer can take passengers directly to their accommodation, while ADO operates buses from Cancún airport’s Terminals 2, 3, and 4 to Tulum . The bus arrives downtown, so travelers staying in the beach hotel zone will need onward transportation.
 Whichever transportation option passengers choose, they should update any existing airport pickup or research a new transfer option before arriving. Lastly, to avoid unexpected costs, particularly given previous reports of excessive taxi charges at Cancún Airport , confirm the total fare and payment currency when booking the ride.
